label: Port / maritime
description: A seaport or terminal: berths and piers, cranes and yard equipment, the terminal operating system, gate operations, vessels, the Coast Guard and the facility security plan. Plans: the Facility Security Plan (33 CFR 105; drills every 3 months, an annual exercise that may be a tabletop), the USCG cyber rule (33 CFR 101 subpart F: Cybersecurity Officer, Cybersecurity Plan, cyber incident response plan, reportable cyber incidents to the National Response Center without delay), and the Area Maritime Security Plan.

vocabulary.facility: the port (berths, piers, yard, gates and the operations center)
vocabulary.public: truckers, passengers, vessel crews and the surrounding community
vocabulary.frontline: crane operators, yard planners, gate clerks, longshore supervisors, vessel agents, harbor patrol

ot: ship-to-shore crane PLCs and vendor remote access
liquid bulk terminal SCADA (tank gauging, valves)

roles.name: Director of Port Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the berths, the yard, the gates and vessel scheduling.

roles.name: Facility Security Officer
roles.description: Owns the facility security plan, access control and the Coast Guard liaison.

roles.name: IT / OT Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the TOS, networks, equipment control and the investigation.

roles.name: Director of External Affairs (PIO)
roles.description: Owns customer notices, social media and the press.

roles.name: Terminal Operator General Manager (Tenant Liaison)
roles.description: Owns the stevedores, the shipping-line customers and the equipment.

roles.name: Cybersecurity Officer
roles.description: Owns the Cybersecurity Plan and cyber incident response plan, and reports cyber incidents to the Coast Guard.

roles.name: Port Police Chief (Harbor Patrol)
roles.description: Owns waterside and landside response and unified command with the USCG and CBP.

roles.name: Emergency Manager
roles.description: Owns the port EOP, heavy-weather plan and Area Maritime Security Plan coordination.

outsideParties: US Coast Guard (Captain of the Port, Sector command center)
the shipping lines and vessel agents
the National Response Center (security and cyber incidents without delay)
NOAA and the US Army Corps of Engineers
the crane OEM and its remote service
a certified state or local counter-UAS law-enforcement team (SAFER SKIES Act authority, in effect since 1 Jul 2026)
mediaChannels: a trucker's post about gate queues on Facebook

sceneAnchors.public: at a ferry or cruise passenger terminal: passengers in queues, bollards and a ship alongside the pier, overcast daylight
sceneAnchors.control: inside a port operations center: operators at consoles in front of a window overlooking container cranes, dark monitors, radios
sceneAnchors.exterior: on a container terminal yard: stacked containers, a gantry crane, a truck lane with a yard tractor, grey water and a ship beyond

noiseExamples: a trucker with an expired appointment
a reefer alarm on a container that is just warm
pressureExamples: a trucker Facebook post about a six-hour gate queue
a shipping line threatening to divert a vessel
a trade reporter asking if the port was hacked
the Captain of the Port asking for a status report
the mayor's office calling about the traffic
the Captain of the Port weighing a COTP order to close the channel
drones over the tank farm and nobody sure whether the Coast Guard or a certified local counter-UAS team acts
